policy: Five independently interpreted UBS Hebrew v0.9.4 headword identities: source-word-specific family approvals for entry-level crosswalk candidates only. Do not treat Strong spelling, H/A prefix, or old SDBH equality alone as equivalence; do not infer contextual sense IDs. These are editorial dispositions, not generated index links. External dictionary web display corroborates sense/context but the pinned original UBS/MACULA metadata is verified by CI. Added twelve distinct named-entity entry reviews grounded in original Ezra/Daniel referents, and preserved context/sense abstention for homonymous names. Published UBS English headword sense glosses are now source-checked as evidence of reviewed *entry* identity, not assigned as any WLC contextual sense; same-Strong and cross-Strong spellings are validated by separate source-bound relations. Third batch: 22 additional exact original-word anchored Hebrew/Aramaic lexical headwords, using original MACULA English witnesses and exact UBS-published gloss membership where independently available. Fourth source-reviewed batch: eleven additional attested lexical entry-only identities from original WLC source word senses and actual UBS published glosses; no automatic sense inference.

decisions.editorial_meaning: Daniel, the protagonist of the book of Daniel
decisions.rationale: UBS headword explicitly has a distinct Daniel-the-book protagonist meaning (Form 1, sense 4) and lists Dan 2:13–20. Source Dan 2:13 refers to that same named figure. The headword can be identified while its contextual sense ID remains unassigned; the headword also records other men named Daniel.

decisions.editorial_meaning: human, human being, man
decisions.rationale: UBS expressly treats this form as human/person and cites Ezra 4:11 and 6:11 alongside Dan 2:10. The original Aramaic word denotes a human, not an unrelated equal-spelling Hebrew homograph.

decisions.editorial_meaning: day, time; days of old
decisions.rationale: The UBS entry covers day/time and specifically documents the Aramaic phrase 'day of old' at Ezra 4:15 and 4:19 (sense 8). The exact original word family corresponds to that headword. Do not infer which sense applies to each of the 16 tokens.

decisions.editorial_meaning: Belshazzar, king of Babylon
decisions.rationale: UBS explicitly identifies the Babylonian king Belshazzar and cites Daniel 5:1–2. The source original token at Daniel 5:1 names that ruler, not Belteshazzar/Daniel.

decisions.editorial_meaning: head of cattle, bull
decisions.rationale: The UBS combined headword explicitly distinguishes Form 5 'head of cattle' with citations Ezra 6:9, 6:17, 7:17 and Daniel 4:25. The original Aramaic source uses the cattle noun. Approve only the containing headword, never automatically choose the unrelated Form 1 'dove' or fabricate a contextual sense.

decisions.editorial_meaning: Israel, the people or nation, as referred to in the Aramaic Ezra 5:1 witness
decisions.rationale: The source says the God of Israel (Ezra 5:1), and UBS identifies the uniquely written Israel headword. The dictionary headword may also encompass the personal name Jacob/Israel; no individual contextual sense is selected.

decisions.editorial_meaning: Cyrus, the Persian king responsible for the rebuilding decree
decisions.rationale: Ezra 5:13 explicitly names Cyrus the king. UBS indexes Cyrus under the same pointed lemma; the different source Strong annotation must not be made a general H/A alias.

decisions.editorial_meaning: Judah, the region or province referred to in Ezra
decisions.rationale: Ezra 5:1–8 concerns the province of Judah, not a separate unrelated personal name. UBS groups the named Jehud/Judah location under this exact indexed headword.

decisions.editorial_meaning: Artaxerxes, the Persian king addressed in Ezra 4
decisions.rationale: Ezra 4:8 and 4:11 explicitly address King Artaxerxes; UBS indexes Artaxerxes with this published original alternate spelling. This entry-level identity does not judge which historically distinct royal titulature or source variant applies.

decisions.editorial_meaning: Media / Medes, named geographical-ethnic referent
decisions.rationale: Ezra 6:2 places the record in Media, and Daniel 5:28 names the Medes. UBS includes Media/Medes under its Madai headword; avoid selecting between person, people and territory senses for the family.

decisions.editorial_meaning: Rehum, royal official named in Ezra 4
decisions.rationale: Rehum is the specifically named official at Ezra 4:8 and 4:9, a referent represented in UBS Rehum's namesake headword. No broader identity merge across other Rehums is approved.

decisions.editorial_meaning: Zechariah, prophet in Ezra 5:1 and 6:14
decisions.rationale: The named prophet Zechariah son of Iddo prophesies alongside Haggai in Ezra 5:1; UBS Zechariah headword includes this named prophet among other people with the same name, whose senses remain distinct.

decisions.editorial_meaning: Haggai, the prophet in Ezra 5:1 and 6:14
decisions.rationale: The prophet Haggai named beside Zechariah in Ezra 5:1 and 6:14 is the person recorded under the UBS Haggai headword. No contextual sense ID transferred.

decisions.editorial_meaning: Moses, associated with priestly duties in Ezra 6:18
decisions.rationale: Ezra 6:18 refers to the written Law of Moses, the biblical leader; UBS Moses headword identifies this name. Do not infer a contextual sense beyond the dictionary entry.

decisions.editorial_meaning: Jeshua, son of Jozadak, in Ezra 5:2
decisions.rationale: Ezra 5:2 names Jeshua together with Zerubbabel and identifies his father Jozadak, supporting the UBS Jeshua headword while preserving distinction from other namesakes.

decisions.editorial_meaning: Jozadak, father of Jeshua, in Ezra 5:2
decisions.rationale: The original Ezra 5:2 occurrence names Jozadak as Jeshua's father; UBS uses the Jozadak/Jehozadak headword for that individual. No conflation with an unrelated similar name.

decisions.editorial_meaning: Hananiah, Daniel's companion, in Daniel 2:17
decisions.rationale: Daniel 2:17 names Hananiah among Daniel's companions, matching UBS Hananiah headword, which can also hold other people with that name; no selection of a contextual sense ID.

decisions.editorial_meaning: Arioch, the captain of Nebuchadnezzar's guard in Daniel 2:14
decisions.rationale: The UBS Arioch headword independently distinguishes the guard captain serving Nebuchadnezzar from the earlier king of Ellasar; the original Daniel 2:14 reference names the guard captain. Approve only the containing headword, not a contextual LEXID.

decisions.editorial_meaning: the Aramaic verb for speaking in Daniel 6:22
decisions.rationale: The original Daniel 6:22 word refers to speaking, and the UBS combined מלל headword explicitly contains a separate verbal meaning 'to speak'. Related withering or circumcision meanings in the same entry are not imported into the original token.

decisions.editorial_meaning: grass / vegetation in Daniel 4:12
decisions.rationale: The Aramaic word in Nebuchadnezzar's tree dream at Daniel 4:12 denotes vegetation; UBS's published source headword contains grass/green plants despite a different Strong annotation.

decisions.editorial_meaning: imprisonment as penalty in Ezra 7:26
decisions.rationale: Ezra 7:26 lists judicial penalties including imprisonment, expressly corresponding to UBS's distinct imprisonment meaning within the shared entry, not to an unrelated name.

decisions.editorial_meaning: lamb offered in Ezra 6:9
decisions.rationale: Ezra 6:9 lists sacrificial animals including lambs; UBS indexes the same Aramaic lexical noun with the lamb meaning, notwithstanding different original Strong/H-A metadata.

decisions.editorial_meaning: tax / tribute at Ezra 4:20
decisions.rationale: Ezra 4:20 discusses tribute and tax payments. UBS's homographic lemma includes a distinct revenue-tax form, not merely measures or giants. The exact dictionary headword can be identified but the individual contextual sense is not assigned.

decisions.editorial_meaning: tax / tribute at Ezra 4:13
decisions.rationale: Ezra 4:13 names required taxes; UBS has a separately attested tax meaning in the published entry. Preserve this exact original suffixed Strong family without generalizing aliases.

decisions.editorial_meaning: food/provisions in Daniel 4:9
decisions.rationale: The source in Daniel 4:9 refers to nourishment provided by the tree; UBS has a food/provisions entry for the same lexical family.

decisions.editorial_meaning: Iddo, ancestor of the prophet Zechariah in Ezra 5:1
decisions.rationale: The name at Ezra 5:1 is Iddo, Zechariah's family ancestor; the UBS Iddo headword explicitly includes that grandfather among several namesakes. No universal name merge or contextual sense transfer.

decisions.editorial_meaning: cord / bond in Job 39:5
decisions.rationale: Job 39:5 uses bonds of the wild donkey, matching UBS's binding-cord meaning despite the source plural/derived orthography and original suffixed Strong variant. This approves only the lexeme entry.

decisions.editorial_meaning: being cast down in Psalm 42:6
decisions.rationale: The psalmist's downcast soul at Psalm 42:6 corresponds semantically to UBS's lower/distressed verb form. Related senses remain unselected; different orthography alone is not treated as a reusable rule.

decisions.editorial_meaning: ancestor of the giants in 2 Samuel 21:16
decisions.rationale: The source names a descendant of Rapha/Raphah among the giant warriors; UBS separately identifies Raphah as ancestor of giants, distinct from other namesakes. Accept headword identity without choosing a LEXID.

decisions.editorial_meaning: Baruch's father Neriah in Jeremiah 36:14
decisions.rationale: Jeremiah 36:14 identifies Neriah in Baruch's family, matching UBS's Neriah entry that explicitly names Baruch as son. Original longer -yahu form remains untouched.

decisions.editorial_meaning: dread/horror in Deuteronomy 28:25
decisions.rationale: The covenant curse in Deuteronomy 28:25 causes horror and dismay; UBS's published lexical meaning is horror, despite the recorded Strong/code and spelling discrepancy.

decisions.editorial_meaning: the slopes by Pisgah in Deuteronomy 3:17
decisions.rationale: Deuteronomy 3:17 uses slope(s) near Pisgah, represented in UBS by a geographical slope/slopes entry. The source word itself is not altered to a different canonical form.

decisions.editorial_meaning: the empty-headed or foolish person in Job 11:12
decisions.rationale: Job 11:12 refers to a senseless person, matching UBS's figurative stupid/hollow meaning rather than a distinct proper name. The original lemma remains unmodified.

decisions.editorial_meaning: sin in Exodus 34:7
decisions.rationale: Exodus 34:7 speaks of the forgiveness of wrongdoing; UBS's same headword includes sin and sin-offering as separate meanings. Accept the word-level headword identity, never automatically assert a contextual LEXID.

decisions.editorial_meaning: Tokhath, father of Shallum and husband of Huldah in 2 Chronicles 34:22
decisions.rationale: The original named Tokhath at 2 Chronicles 34:22 is the father of Shallum. The UBS תִּקְוָה headword explicitly describes that man as 'also known as Tokhath' in its Tikvah personal-name meaning; a word-anchored headword equivalence is justified without transferring UBS contextual LEXID.

decisions.editorial_meaning: Samuel's Ramathaim-Zophim, associated with the UBS Ramah settlement in Ephraim
decisions.rationale: 1 Samuel 1:1 identifies Ramathaim Zophim, Samuel's place of origin. A UBS רָמָה location meaning explicitly states that its Ephraim settlement is 'also known as Ramathaim or Ramathaim Zophim'; this accepts only the UBS combined headword, not a generic Strong alias.

decisions.editorial_meaning: En-Tannin or Dragon Spring outside Jerusalem in Nehemiah 2:13
decisions.rationale: The original Nehemiah 2:13 named spring is glossed 'the Well of the Dragons' in pinned WLC, and the UBS entry עֵין הַתַּנִּין explicitly identifies En-Tannin / Dragon Spring at Nehemiah 2:13. The full referent agrees, but the independently segmented morphology and original Strong remain unchanged.

decisions.editorial_meaning: Sheol / the realm of the dead in Isaiah 7:11's contrast between depth and height
decisions.rationale: In Isaiah 7:11 the original WLC English witness is 'sheol' at 'make it deep as Sheol, or high as heaven'. The UBS שְׁאוֹל indexed headword explicitly denotes the world of the dead. The original lemma and textual gloss are preserved; only the entry-level identity is corroborated without contextual LEXID inference.

decisions.editorial_meaning: The temple construction was completed in Ezra 6:15
decisions.rationale: Ezra 6:15 explicitly states that the temple was completed. The UBS יצא verb includes its own independently published 'to be completed' lexical meaning. The Aramaic source Strong/word ID remains unchanged, and no universal H/A alias is introduced.

decisions.editorial_meaning: Israel's priests will boast in the riches of the nations (Isaiah 61:6)
decisions.rationale: Isaiah 61:6 uses the original verb in the sense of boasting. UBS אמר includes an explicit 'to boast' meaning, corroborating the contextual headword without selecting its LEXID.

decisions.editorial_meaning: Judah's towns are desolated by young lions in Jeremiah 2:15
decisions.rationale: Jeremiah 2:15 says the cities have been ruined/desolated. UBS נצה explicitly includes 'to be desolated', so the identity of this particular lexical headword is corroborated; original lemma and composite source SDBH are untouched.

decisions.editorial_meaning: The giant of great stature in 2 Samuel 21:20
decisions.rationale: 2 Samuel 21:20 speaks of a person of unusual stature with six fingers and toes; UBS מִדָּה specifically has 'man of stature'/'giant' as a published lexical meaning. The source's gloss 'great' is contextually compatible with that entry but no sense ID is transferred.

decisions.editorial_meaning: The first original Aramaic name element Jegar in Jegar-Sahadutha (Genesis 31:47)
decisions.rationale: Genesis 31:47 names the memorial Jegar-Sahadutha with the original source segment יְגַר and separately linked second original segment. The pinned UBS edition deliberately indexes יְגַר as its own exact canonical headword with the gloss Jegar-Sahadutha; this permits the specific entry-only identity, not a fabricated contextual sense or a global Strong alias.

decisions.editorial_meaning: The second original Aramaic name element Sahadutha in Jegar-Sahadutha (Genesis 31:47)
decisions.rationale: Genesis 31:47 supplies the second Aramaic segment שָׂהֲדוּ of the named memorial Jegar-Sahadutha. UBS indexes that same original lemma in a separate published headword glossed Jegar-Sahadutha. No identity between the two distinct UBS entries is inferred; only this segment's specific entry is reviewed.

decisions.editorial_meaning: The psalmist's grief/affliction in Psalm 77:11
decisions.rationale: Psalm 77:11 has the original verbal form with source English grief. UBS חלל includes the published lexical meaning 'to grieve', supporting this word's entry-level identification while its specific contextual UBS sense remains unassigned.

decisions.editorial_meaning: Fear in Isaiah 44:8, addressed to the Lord's witnesses
decisions.rationale: The original Isaiah 44:8 word is 'afraid' in pinned WLC, and UBS ירה explicitly has a sense 'to be afraid'. The original H7297a Strong and source SDBH are preserved, never promoted as global equivalents of UBS H3384.

decisions.editorial_meaning: The plural grinders who cease in Ecclesiastes 12:3
decisions.rationale: Ecclesiastes 12:3 uses טֹחֲנֹות as a substantivized feminine plural grinding agent ('grinders'). The published UBS טחן verbal headword means 'to grind' and shares the original numeric Strong family; this source morphology supports the lexical root at entry level, not a claim that the original noun and dictionary verb have identical POS or contextual sense.

decisions.editorial_meaning: Cypress/fir wood used in the Tyrian ship fittings in Ezekiel 27:6
decisions.rationale: Ezekiel 27:6 describes wood of 'cypresses' in the original MACULA English witness. UBS תְּאַשּׁוּר includes the source-published gloss 'cypress' under the same numeric Strong family. This confirms the broad lexical tree headword only; species-specific determination is explicitly not inferred.
